motifs.label: Forcing Mate
motifs.evidence: Qxc6+ starts a forced mating attack. Every legal defence permits mate within 3 moves; one verified line is Qxc6+ Qd7 Qxa8+ Qc8 Qxc8#. The exact continuation depends on the defence.

motifs.label: Checkmate
motifs.evidence: Qxc8# is checkmate: the king is in check and there is no legal reply.

motifs.label: Hanging Piece
motifs.evidence: Qxc6+ wins the loose knight on c6.

motifs.label: Discovered Attack
motifs.evidence: Bxg5+ vacates d8, uncovering the rook on f8 against the queen on a8. The moving bishop gives check, so the opponent cannot simply ignore the exposed attack. Every legal reply concedes material. Captures and interpositions are included in this check.

motifs.label: Forcing Attack
motifs.evidence: Qh5+ starts a checking attack that wins material or mates against every legal reply. After g6, Bc4+ d5 Qxd5+ Ke8 Qxd8+ wins material. The continuation depends on the defence; later pins and forks belong to their actual positions, not the opening check.

motifs.label: Trapped Rook
motifs.evidence: Qxb7 attacks the rook on a8. It has no safe move, including captures. Defending it also concedes material: Bd5 is answered by Nxd5. Every legal defence loses material through the trapped piece or its defender. This wins additional material beyond the initial capture.

timeline.label: Winning Recapture
timeline.evidence: Qxd5+ wins the queen on d5 in exchange for the bishop just captured there. The settled local exchange gains 5.7 pawns of material; this is the payoff, not a newly hanging piece.
